Hey guys, welcome back to my channel!
Today I want to talk a little bit about saving money on groceries.
So groceries are really expensive right now, as I'm sure you all know.
Anyway, there are a few things you can do.
You can make a list before you go to the store.
You can also buy things on sale.
And you can try not to go shopping when you're hungry, that's a big one.
So yeah, those are some tips.
Let me know what you think in the comments and don't forget to like and subscribe!

I cut my grocery bill from $600 to $310 without clipping a single coupon.
[receipt comparison on screen]
The first trick sounds boring: I shop with a list. But the list isn't the trick.
The trick is I write it after checking what's already in my fridge. That alone killed $80 of duplicate buys.
Second: I stopped buying pre-cut anything. Same carrots, triple the price.
But the biggest drop came from one rule I almost didn't try.
I never shop more than once a week. Every extra trip cost me about $40 in 'while I'm here' items.
$290 a month back. That's a flight every quarter.
Comment your monthly grocery bill and I'll tell you where it's leaking.

Did you know that Napoleon wasn't actually short?
He was about 5 foot 7, which was average for a Frenchman at the time.
The myth started partly because French inches were longer than English inches.
So when the British read 5 foot 2, they thought he was tiny.
Also, British cartoonists loved drawing him as a little angry man.
And his nickname, le petit caporal, was actually a term of affection, not about height.
So Napoleon was completely normal height.
Follow for more history facts.

Napoleon was taller than the average Frenchman. So why do we all think he was tiny?
Blame a unit conversion.
His height was recorded as 5 foot 2 - in French inches, which were longer than English ones.
Converted, that's about 5 foot 7. Perfectly average.
But the British didn't convert it. They just read '5 foot 2' and ran with it.
And their cartoonists made it stick: every newspaper drew him as a tiny man throwing tantrums.
Here's the part that stings: even his nickname helped the lie.
Le petit caporal - 'the little corporal' - was what his soldiers called him out of love.
One rounding error and a few cartoons, and he's been short for 200 years.

So in this video I'm going to be talking about protein.
Protein is a macronutrient that is super important for your body and it does a lot of things.
Basically what protein does is it helps with muscle protein synthesis which is the process of building muscle, and also it has other functions as well that are important.
The recommended amount varies depending on a lot of different factors like your weight and your activity level and your goals and other things.
So it's really important to get enough protein.
It's super important.
So make sure you're getting enough protein every day.
Thanks for watching.

Three mistakes that are killing your gains.
Number one: not eating enough protein. Aim for about 1.6 grams per kilo of body weight.
Number two: skipping sleep. Your muscles grow when you rest, not when you train.
Number three: changing your program every week. Stick with one plan for at least 8 weeks.
Fix these and you'll see results.
Save this for your next gym session.

Your phone is lying to you about its battery.
[close-up of battery at 1%]
That 1% isn't 1%. Manufacturers keep a hidden reserve so the phone can shut down safely.
Which is why it sometimes hangs on 1% for ten minutes.
But the reserve isn't the real problem.
The real problem is you charging to 100% every night.
Lithium batteries wear fastest when they sit full. Keep yours between 20 and 80 and it ages noticeably slower.
Both iPhone and most Androids have a setting that does this for you. It's called optimized or adaptive charging.
Turn it on tonight. Your battery in two years will thank you.

Stop throwing out your stale bread. It's about to become the best thing you cook this week.
[bread thrown on a cutting board]
Cut it into cubes, toss with olive oil, salt and garlic.
Bake at 200 degrees for 12 minutes.
You can also use it for bread pudding, or breadcrumbs, or French toast, or panzanella, which is an Italian salad.
There are honestly so many things you can do with stale bread.
I also sometimes freeze bread, that works too.
Anyway, yeah.
